learningObjective: Distinguish expert parallelism (EP) and sequence parallelism (SP) from TP/PP and identify their communication primitives.

canonicalClaims.claim: EP places different MoE experts on different devices; routing uses all-to-all to shuffle tokens to experts and again to bring results back. SP shards intermediate activations along the sequence axis inside a TP region; it uses AllGather / ReduceScatter to bridge the TP and SP regions, primarily to reduce activation memory.
conditions: MoE model for EP; TP-parallel model for SP.
Communication library supports all-to-all / AllGather / ReduceScatter.
nonImplications: Does not imply EP and SP are equivalent.
Does not imply SP reduces KV cache; SP addresses activation memory during forward.

misconceptions.claim: EP and SP both use a single AllReduce like TP.
misconceptions.whyWrong: EP uses all-to-all; SP uses AllGather/ReduceScatter.

misconceptions.claim: SP reduces KV cache size by sharding along the sequence axis.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SP addresses activation memory; KV cache is a separate resource.
vLLM, TRT-LLM, and DeepSpeed all support EP in inference.

implementationFacts: EP is often combined with TP within a node (TP for attention/MLP inside expert, EP across experts).
SP is a 'free' memory reduction with modest AllGather overhead in Megatron-LM's design.
performanceScenarios: EP scales MoE inference across nodes because it distributes the parameter footprint.
SP is most useful in long-context training where activation memory dominates.
